scope: One DEV parent, two saved noises, two physical-surface-equivalent representations, three models and two stages. Every page and all 24 output cells were actually viewed.

definitions.adoption: Plausibility of using blue C in the supplied seating-surface role, not exact vertex connectivity.
definitions.body: Visible completeness and coherence, including unresolved multi-level organization; a different reasonable style is allowed.
definitions.support: Whether substantial major support elements are visible; sparse thin remnants are UNCERTAIN, not automatically MISSING.
definitions.fragment_evidence: Image evidence for fragments/gaps; fixed-section endpoints alone are insufficient. Body impairment may be clear while disconnected-component status remains uncertain.

limitations: Nonblind AI_PROXY review, not human certification.
The reviewer separately summarized frozen numerical comparisons, but did not inspect candidate numerical metric tables to assign these labels.
All displayed output labels and rendering captions were visible.
Fine topological contacts, illegal overlap and disconnected-fragment counts cannot be certified from these views.
Backless designs are allowed; negative adoption judgments concern the gray upper top replacing the blue surface's apparent seating role, not absence of a back alone.

summary: FLIP200 locally retains the broad-ended bench organization for n0 under EDGE_FLIP, whereas PLAIN200 changes to an elevated gray top and then a sparse final frame. This is a local stability/shape-retention signal, not a newly certified C-adoption success: the original n0 contact ambiguity persists. For n1, both continued models and both representations place gray structure above blue C, and their FINAL bodies become visibly depleted; EXPOSURE retains a plausible seat/back arrangement. Thus the local n0 benefit coexists with an n1 quality cost. No detached-component count is inferred from short section lines.
